structure: A mandatory; B one of two; C one of two

items.prompt_en: Calculate Nerava’s Year B trade balance in goods and services. Show the method and state whether it is a deficit or surplus.
requirements_en: Select the appropriate figures from the supplied source.
Show the calculation and classify the resulting balance correctly.

items.prompt_en: Explain why the improvement in the goods and services trade balance cannot by itself establish whether Nerava has a current account surplus.
requirements_en: Distinguish the goods-and-services trade balance from the current account.
Identify other current-account information needed before making a conclusion.

items.prompt_en: Analyse two channels through which depreciation could change Nerava’s trade balance over time. Refer to the source.
requirements_en: Analyse two distinct mechanisms affecting export/import prices, quantities or receipts.
Use evidence from the source and recognise how effects may change over time.

items.prompt_en: Assess whether vocational training is likely to do more than exchange-rate intervention to improve Nerava’s long-run growth and external trade position.
requirements_en: Explain appropriate channels linking training and exchange-rate intervention to output, competitiveness and trade.
Analyse relevant costs, time lags and source conditions.
Develop a conditional and supported comparative judgement.

items.prompt_en: Assess whether an oligopolistic market is necessarily less economically efficient than a perfectly competitive market.
requirements_en: Use relevant concepts of allocative, productive and dynamic efficiency.
Compare important market characteristics and incentives.
Analyse efficiency losses from market power and potential gains from economies of scale or innovation.
Evaluate whether the claim holds in every case and justify the conclusion.

items.prompt_en: Evaluate whether an indirect tax is the most effective government response to a negative externality arising from industrial production.
requirements_en: Apply relevant external-cost analysis to explain the market failure.
Analyse likely effects and limitations of an indirect tax.
Compare at least one defensible alternative intervention and reach a conditional judgement.

items.prompt_en: Assess the extent to which monetary policy can achieve sustained economic growth in an open economy without worsening inflation.
requirements_en: Explain monetary-policy transmission through economic demand, interest rates and exchange rates.
Distinguish short-run demand effects from sustained growth in productive capacity.
Evaluate trade-offs, constraints, inflation and time lags in an open economy.

items.prompt_en: Evaluate the view that real GDP per head should be the primary measure used to judge a country’s economic development.
requirements_en: Explain what real GDP per head captures and why it is used.
Analyse limitations including inequality, wider welfare and sustainability.
Compare with suitable additional development indicators and reach a supported judgement.
